lines.text: # End honestly, and in more than one way
A Campaign ends in facts. There are exactly three honest ways for one to end, and a generation limit
is not among them.
1. **The Goal is met.** The target was reached and the constraints hold, stated with the values and
the citations that say so.
2. **The exploration converged.** The moves stopped changing anything: the value the Loop converges
on stayed inside the declared band across the declared number of generations. "Converged" is a
measurement, not a mood — the pack declares which value and which band.
3. **An ending the pack declares in its own words.** Something in the business said stop, and the
pack said in advance what that would be: a gate the library tool refuses to pass, adoption that
stayed at zero, an input the flow rejects, a stage that cannot run on this Site at all.
**A generation limit is a budget, not an ending.** When a Campaign stops because it ran out of
generations, nobody knows what happened: the method may have been converging slowly, or it may have
been walking away from the answer for its whole life. An ending nobody can explain is the one thing a
Campaign must not deliver, because the whole promise is that it ends in facts.
## What this means for a pack you are authoring
- **Write the `Endings` section first, not last.** Every way this business can stop, in the words a
person would use. If you cannot name three, you do not yet know the business well enough to author
the pack.
- **Every declared ending needs the value that detects it.** An ending that no reader produces a
number for is an ending the runner can never reach. If the pack says "stop when the library gate
fails", some reader has to report whether the gate failed.
- **Convergence is stated in the chooser's own vocabulary.** The value converged on has to be one
the chooser actually reads; a pack that converges on a number its chooser never looks at can only
ever end at its limit.
- **The generation limit stays, and stays a budget.** It protects the Site and the person's time. It
should be reached only when something is wrong, and when it is reached the report says so plainly
rather than dressing it up as a conclusion.
- **Say what a person must never have to guess.** If a stop can be read two ways — met exactly, or
not measured at all — the pack's words must distinguish them on every face.
## Citing it
When this file shaped a decision, cite it by name and say what it changed — "made every ending one
this pack declares in words, and added the reader that detects the library gate's refusal".

2: 
3: A verification session answers the question its options asked, not the question you meant. The same
4: tool, on the same data, with a different rule deck, a different cell view, a different set of checks
5: enabled or a different severity threshold, will answer "clean" and "not clean" with equal confidence
6: — and both answers are correct for what was actually asked.
7: 
8: **So a run whose options were not asserted has not verified anything.** It has produced a number
9: whose meaning nobody can state afterwards, and a pass obtained under the wrong options is worse than
10: a failure: it is a failure that looks like success and travels into a report as a fact.
11:

13: 
14: - **Declare the options in the pack, beside the constraint they serve.** Which checks, which rule
15:   set, which views, which thresholds. Not "the usual ones" — the list, written down.
16: - **Assert them at run time, before the count is read.** The session must be made to state the
17:   options it ran under, and a reader must hold that statement against the declaration. If the two
18:   disagree, the generation has no verdict: it has a blocker, and the pack says so in words.
19: - **Make the assertion a typed value, not a comment.** "Options as declared: yes/no", plus the list
20:   the session reported, so the judge can cite it and a person reading the report six months later can
21:   see exactly what was checked.
22: - **Never infer the options from the result.** A clean result is not evidence that the right checks
23:   ran; it is equally consistent with no checks having run at all.
24: - **Record the tool's own version beside them.** Options mean different things across versions, and a
25:   Campaign compared against an earlier one has to be able to say whether that comparison is fair.

28: 
29: A generation passes; the report says the design is clean; the option set had one whole class of check
30: switched off. Nothing in the ledger is wrong — every number is what the tool said — and the
31: conclusion is false. There is no way to detect this later from the numbers alone, which is why the
32: assertion has to happen before the count is read rather than after the campaign is over.

tool, on the same data, with a different rule deck, a different cell view, a different set of checks
enabled or a different severity threshold, will answer "clean" and "not clean" with equal confidence
— and both answers are correct for what was actually asked.

whose meaning nobody can state afterwards, and a pass obtained under the wrong options is worse than
a failure: it is a failure that looks like success and travels into a report as a fact.
## What this means for a pack you are authoring

set, which views, which thresholds. Not "the usual ones" — the list, written down.

ran; it is equally consistent with no checks having run at all.

1: # One verification tool per session
2: 
3: A count belongs to one tool and one option set. Run two verification tools in one session and the
4: violation count that comes out belongs to neither: you cannot say which tool found what, you cannot
5: compare the number against a run of either tool alone, and you cannot re-run half of it.
6: 
7: **So a session runs one verification tool.** Not one *kind* of tool — one tool. If the business needs
8: two, that is two act nodes, two sessions, two reports and two typed values.
9: 
10: ## What this means for a pack you are authoring
11: 
12: - **One act node per verification tool.** Each node launches its own session, produces its own
13:   report, and its report is read by its own reader into its own named value. The node's name says
14:   which tool it is.
15: - **Name the values after what produced them.** Two values both called "violations" will be compared
16:   by somebody. Give each the tool's name in its own name, and its unit and meaning in the pack's
17:   `Semantics`.
18: - **Do not sum across tools.** A total over two tools' counts is a number with no unit and no owner.
19:   If the business wants one verdict, the judge takes it from a rule over the two named values, and
20:   the rule says in words how the two combine.
21: - **Fork rather than fold.** Two verification tools that can run at once are two branches of a fork
22:   that converge into a judge node — that is what fork and join are for, and it keeps each count
23:   attached to the session that produced it.
24: - **One session, one option set.** The companion rule is in `assert-the-checker-options.md`: a
25:   session whose options were not asserted has verified nothing, and a session running two tools
26:   cannot have one asserted option set at all.
27: 
28: ## The failure this prevents
29: 
30: A single session runs two tools to save a licence checkout; the report carries one count; six months
31: later a person asks which tool found the seventeen violations and no record can answer. The Campaign
32: ended in a number rather than in facts.
33: 
34: ## Citing it
35: 
36: When this file shaped a decision, cite it by name and say what it changed — "split the one
37: verification node into two, one per tool, each with its own reader and its own named count, joined at
38: a judge node".

(End of file - total 38 lines)
</content>

- **Name the values after what produced them.** Two values both called "violations" will be compared
by somebody. Give each the tool's name in its own name, and its unit and meaning in the pack's
`Semantics`.
- **Do not sum across tools.** A total over two tools' counts is a number with no unit and no owner.
If the business wants one verdict, the judge takes it from a rule over the two named values, and
the rule says in words how the two combine.
- **Fork rather than fold.** Two verification tools that can run at once are two branches of a fork
that converge into a judge node — that is what fork and join are for, and it keeps each count
attached to the session that produced it.
- **One session, one option set.** The companion rule is in `assert-the-checker-options.md`: a
session whose options were not asserted has verified nothing, and a session running two tools
cannot have one asserted option set at all.
## The failure this prevents
A single session runs two tools to save a licence checkout; the report carries one count; six months
later a person asks which tool found the seventeen violations and no record can answer. The Campaign
ended in a number rather than in facts.
## Citing it
When this file shaped a decision, cite it by name and say what it changed — "split the one
verification node into two, one per tool, each with its own reader and its own named count, joined at
a judge node".

that binds to any Site meeting its contract; a pack carrying a copy of one Site's flow is a pack

there**, as pointers.

file first: it names the stages and the variables each one takes, and a variable a stage takes on
the command line is a knob a generation can set without editing anything.

takes" is a pointer. A pasted copy of the file is an import, and it goes stale the first time
somebody edits the real one.

author may know something the flow does not encode. Ask, and record how it was settled.

preparation makes its own copy of the pieces the contract names, so a generation never writes into
the reference. That is the runner's job and it is already done.

the path is not readable, say so and stop. A pack authored from a description of a flow nobody
looked at is a pack of guesses.

# Pack intent: library-authoring-qualification

## Business

**Scope, stated once and repeated in the specification and the test record.** This Pack performs one bounded local authoring-qualification check of one local JSON input, and nothing else. It checks only that a source contract was present and read. It does not invoke Liberty, does not invoke QuaLib, does not call `edarun`, uses no production Library facts, requalifies no Wave 2 E1--E4 method, touches no customer data, and therefore claims no commercial qualification. A PASS is not qualification of any Library. The customer-facing wording must say that native QuaLib qualification, production Library facts and Wave 2 E1--E4 claims are outside this Pack's TEST.

**What is explored.** Nothing varies. One generation re-runs the same fixed input through the same two commands; the flow exposes no knob that changes what is checked. The input is one JSON file and its 64-hex `sourceSha256`, fixed before the Run and immutable for it, so a different input is a new Campaign rather than a second generation. The unit of exploration is therefore the single bounded contract check itself, not a swept or stepped quantity.

**What is measured.** Exactly one reading: `library_contract_ready`, unit `count`, written only by the flow's own reader (`read-library-contract.py`) into the Pack output declared exactly as `libraryContract`. Its value is `1` only after every required field validates: the 64-character hexadecimal `sourceSha256`, the literal `qualification` value `authoring-qualification`, the envelope `schema` `hima-library-insight-report/1`, a non-empty `provenance` string, and an explicit non-empty list of non-blank `unknowns`. The reading means "this bounded source contract was present and read" and nothing more: not Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality or customer value. There is no second number, no ratio, no derived percentage and no denominator.

**The two ordered rules.** Both rules read that one value, constraint first and goal second: constraint `library-contract-nonnegative` requires `library_contract_ready >= 0 count`; goal `library-contract-goal` requires the same reading against the bound goal of `1 count`. The distinction between a valid zero-or-greater constraint reading and the requested success target is preserved on every face.

**What ends it, in this Pack's own words.** Three honest endings:
1. *Goal met.* Constraint PASS and goal PASS, and only then does the explicit Explore `decide` record `goalMet` and end the Run. Only PASS/PASS may produce this ending.
2. *Refused input.* The input is invalid or absent: the flow refuses it (no envelope is written, no numeric value exists) or the reader refuses the envelope, so no count exists and no rule can pass. The Run ends stating which required field was missing, malformed or blank, and that there is no success value.
3. *Valid but not ready.* A validated envelope carrying `0 count`: constraint PASS, goal FAIL. The Run ends as not-ready and is never converted into a goal result.

A FAIL or an unknown on either rule goes to the same declared refusal path and never becomes a goal result. The generation/retry/time budget is a budget, not an ending: if it is ever reached, the report says plainly that the budget was exhausted with no conclusion, and it is not dressed up as one of the three endings above.

**What a person must never have to guess.**
- Whether an absent number means *refused* or *measured zero*. The refusal ending must name the missing, malformed or blank field and say that no success value exists; the not-ready ending must state the typed value `0 count`, so a missing number and a true zero can never be read as the same thing.
- Whether a constraint PASS says anything about Library quality. It does not: `>= 0 count` is a presence and non-negativity gate, and from this flow it can only PASS or be UNDETERMINED.
- Whether `goalMet` means the local bounded contract was present (it does) rather than that a Library was qualified (it does not).
- Whether the Run was already terminal before a TEST record was written. The SOP allows a TEST record only after that explicit decision has made the Run terminal; a running or paused Run is not TEST evidence.
- Which name means what: the Pack output `libraryContract` versus the typed reading `library_contract_ready` versus the rule ids `library-contract-*`, and the input field `reportSchema` versus the envelope field `schema` that the first command writes in its place.

**Input, feedback and budget boundary.**
- *Input identity:* one local JSON input file (the flow ships `library-input.json`) plus its 64-hex `sourceSha256`; immutable for the Campaign, and a changed input starts a new Campaign.
- *Feedback that may change the next move:* none. There is one generation, no strategy knob, no chooser that re-aims the check.
- *Budget:* 1 generation; 1 retry covering only an execution or transport fault (one attempt, never a second measurement that replaces a first); 300 s wall clock; Site `local` offers 1 parallel Job and zero licence seats, so one Job at a time and no licence checkout; no commercial EDA is invoked. A refused input is final and is never retried.

**Counterexamples the later readers and rules must survive.** These are test input, read from the flow, and they are not a claim that any commercial flow has passed.
- Empty file or `{}` -- `analyze-library-contract.sh` raises through its Python heredoc (parse or type check fails): non-zero exit, no envelope, no numeric value. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 10--22.
- Missing `unknowns`, an empty list, or a blank/non-string item -- the same refusal with the message `invalid local Library authoring-qualification input`. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 19--22.
- Blank or non-string `provenance` -- the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, line 18.
- Malformed or non-64-hex `sourceSha256` -- the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 14--15.
- Wrong `qualification` label or wrong `reportSchema` -- the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 16--17.
- A present envelope failing the reader's own five-field check -- `read-library-contract.py` exits non-zero with `invalid local Library authoring-qualification result` and writes no observation value. Source: `flow/read-library-contract.py`, lines 8--20.
- The shipped placeholder identity `aaaa...a` -- format-valid, so it passes every check and yields the typed value `library_contract_ready = 1 count`. It is the counterexample that stops that count being quoted as "the source identity was verified", because it is the digest of nothing. Source: `flow/library-input.json`, line 2.
- A valid envelope carrying `0 count` -- a declared test input, not producible by this flow's reader (which emits `1` or refuses): constraint PASS, goal FAIL, declared not-ready ending. A true zero must never be read as success.
- Two candidate results, or an extra opaque success key at the reader's envelope -- dropped by reconstruction rather than refused: the first command rebuilds the envelope from exactly its five keys and the reader ignores anything else, so extras are invisible. Declared limit: this Pack's refusal claim covers missing, malformed and blank fields only.

- Flow root, read in place with read tools and never copied into this Pack: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-AT8h3n/hima-home-OzRhpJ/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow`

- Declared identities of the three sources, as handed off (`SOP.md` sha256 `ae7217528756594ed7629d005912d84bf50bb27587fdf07af582eb2376491508`, 1881 bytes; `qualification-requirements.md` sha256 `bbfceececefa28d293c281c93f631403b0ec5a8d596b65c5494caf49b95f3f90`, 1204 bytes; `report-requirements.md` sha256 `41b01f43906a6ff46b33639f2df5a15bf63eb0697439b086852b65089208428b`, 475 bytes): declared, and deliberately recorded as unverified here because this authoring session has no shell and cannot recompute a digest, so no digest is claimed as re-verified.

# Pack intent: library-authoring-qualification

## Business

**Scope, stated once and repeated in the specification and the test record.** This Pack performs one bounded local authoring-qualification check of one local JSON input, and nothing else. It checks only that a source contract was present and read. It does not invoke Liberty, does not invoke QuaLib, does not call `edarun`, uses no production Library facts, requalifies no Wave 2 E1--E4 method, touches no customer data, and therefore claims no commercial qualification. A PASS is not qualification of any Library. The customer-facing wording must say that native QuaLib qualification, production Library facts and Wave 2 E1--E4 claims are outside this Pack's TEST.

**What is explored.** Nothing varies. One generation re-runs the same fixed input through the same two commands; the flow exposes no knob that changes what is checked. The input is one JSON file and its 64-hex `sourceSha256`, fixed before the Run and immutable for it, so a different input is a new Campaign rather than a second generation. The unit of exploration is therefore the single bounded contract check itself, not a swept or stepped quantity.

**What is measured.** Exactly one reading: `library_contract_ready`, unit `count`, written only by the flow's own reader (`read-library-contract.py`) into the Pack output declared exactly as `libraryContract`. Its value is `1` only after every required field validates: the 64-character hexadecimal `sourceSha256`, the literal `qualification` value `authoring-qualification`, the envelope `schema` `hima-library-insight-report/1`, a non-empty `provenance` string, and an explicit non-empty list of non-blank `unknowns`. The reading means "this bounded source contract was present and read" and nothing more: not Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality or customer value. There is no second number, no ratio, no derived percentage and no denominator.

**The two ordered rules.** Both rules read that one value, constraint first and goal second: constraint `library-contract-nonnegative` requires `library_contract_ready >= 0 count`; goal `library-contract-goal` requires the same reading against the bound goal of `1 count`. The distinction between a valid zero-or-greater constraint reading and the requested success target is preserved on every face.

**What ends it, in this Pack's own words.** Three honest endings:
1. *Goal met.* Constraint PASS and goal PASS, and only then does the explicit Explore `decide` record `goalMet` and end the Run. Only PASS/PASS may produce this ending.
2. *Refused input.* The input is invalid or absent: the flow refuses it (no envelope is written, no numeric value exists) or the reader refuses the envelope, so no count exists and no rule can pass. The Run ends stating which required field was missing, malformed or blank, and that there is no success value.
3. *Valid but not ready.* A validated envelope carrying `0 count`: constraint PASS, goal FAIL. The Run ends as not-ready and is never converted into a goal result.

A FAIL or an unknown on either rule goes to the same declared refusal path and never becomes a goal result. The generation/retry/time budget is a budget, not an ending: if it is ever reached, the report says plainly that the budget was exhausted with no conclusion, and it is not dressed up as one of the three endings above.

**What a person must never have to guess.**
- Whether an absent number means *refused* or *measured zero*. The refusal ending must name the missing, malformed or blank field and say that no success value exists; the not-ready ending must state the typed value `0 count`, so a missing number and a true zero can never be read as the same thing.
- Whether a constraint PASS says anything about Library quality. It does not: `>= 0 count` is a presence and non-negativity gate, and from this flow it can only PASS or be UNDETERMINED.
- Whether `goalMet` means the local bounded contract was present (it does) rather than that a Library was qualified (it does not).
- Whether the Run was already terminal before a TEST record was written. The SOP allows a TEST record only after that explicit decision has made the Run terminal; a running or paused Run is not TEST evidence.
- Which name means what: the Pack output `libraryContract` versus the typed reading `library_contract_ready` versus the rule ids `library-contract-*`, and the input field `reportSchema` versus the envelope field `schema` that the first command writes in its place.

**Input, feedback and budget boundary.**
- *Input identity:* one local JSON input file (the flow ships `library-input.json`) plus its 64-hex `sourceSha256`; immutable for the Campaign, and a changed input starts a new Campaign.
- *Feedback that may change the next move:* none. There is one generation, no strategy knob, no chooser that re-aims the check.
- *Budget:* 1 generation; 1 retry covering only an execution or transport fault (one attempt, never a second measurement that replaces a first); 300 s wall clock; Site `local` offers 1 parallel Job and zero licence seats, so one Job at a time and no licence checkout; no commercial EDA is invoked. A refused input is final and is never retried.

**Counterexamples the later readers and rules must survive.** These are test input, read from the flow, and they are not a claim that any commercial flow has passed.
- Empty file or `{}` -- `analyze-library-contract.sh` raises through its Python heredoc (parse or type check fails): non-zero exit, no envelope, no numeric value. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 10--22.
- Missing `unknowns`, an empty list, or a blank/non-string item -- the same refusal with the message `invalid local Library authoring-qualification input`. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 19--22.
- Blank or non-string `provenance` -- the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, line 18.
- Malformed or non-64-hex `sourceSha256` -- the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 14--15.
- Wrong `qualification` label or wrong `reportSchema` -- the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 16--17.
- A present envelope failing the reader's own five-field check -- `read-library-contract.py` exits non-zero with `invalid local Library authoring-qualification result` and writes no observation value. Source: `flow/read-library-contract.py`, lines 8--20.
- The shipped placeholder identity `aaaa...a` -- format-valid, so it passes every check and yields the typed value `library_contract_ready = 1 count`. It is the counterexample that stops that count being quoted as "the source identity was verified", because it is the digest of nothing. Source: `flow/library-input.json`, line 2.
- A valid envelope carrying `0 count` -- a declared test input, not producible by this flow's reader (which emits `1` or refuses): constraint PASS, goal FAIL, declared not-ready ending. A true zero must never be read as success.

## Goal template

**Primary target:** `library_contract_ready`, bound goal `1 count` — the reading carried by the declared output `libraryContract`.

- **Target name:** `library_contract_ready`.
- **Bound goal:** `1`.
- **Unit:** `count`.
- **What it means:** the one bounded local authoring-qualification input was read and its identity, schema, qualification label, provenance and explicit unknowns all validated. It means "this bounded source contract was present and read" and nothing else — not Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality or customer value, and not commercial qualification.
- **Parameters a Campaign fixes:** the input identity — one local JSON file plus the 64-hex `sourceSha256` it carries — fixed before the Run and immutable for it. There is no strategy knob, so nothing else is parameterized and no second target is declared.
- **What it is not:** a Library measurement of any kind; the Pack's own words for the scope it may claim are kept in the Pack knowledge file `knowledge/scope-and-limits.md`.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which made the target a value a reader actually produces, so the ending that claims it can be reached by measurement; and by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`, which kept the requested target (`1 count`) distinct from the constraint reading so a constraint PASS is never promoted into the target.

## Constraints

**Every constraint the Goal carries, typed and checkable.**

- **Constraint `library-contract-nonnegative`** — `library_contract_ready >= 0 count`. Type: count, lower bound 0. Checkable by the Judge rule of the same id. It is deliberately a presence and non-negativity gate: from this flow's reader the reading is `1` or absent, so this constraint can PASS or be UNDETERMINED and its FAIL is unreachable (declared limit).
- **Goal binding `library-contract-goal`** — the same reading against the bound goal `1 count`. Type: count, bound 1. Checkable by the Judge rule of the same id.

**The options this measurement was made under, declared and asserted before the count is read.**

1. Stage one exactly: `sh analyze-library-contract.sh library-input.json library-insight.json`.
2. Stage two exactly: `python3 read-library-contract.py library-insight.json observation.json`.
3. Five required input fields, validated by both stages: `sourceSha256` as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters; `qualification` equal to `authoring-qualification`; `reportSchema` equal to `hima-library-insight-report/1`; `provenance` a non-blank string; `unknowns` a non-empty list of non-blank strings.
4. The envelope is exactly the five keys stage one writes, with the input's `reportSchema` carried as `schema`.
5. One reader — the flow's `read-library-contract.py` — one option set, one value.

A reading means something only under exactly this option set; the reader's own gate asserts it and refuses anything else, so a `1` is never taken as evidence that the right fields were checked. A separate typed "options as declared: yes/no" value would be a second reading the author did not ask for and the flow's reader does not produce, so none is written: the assertion lives in the reader's refusal, and a reading made under other options has no verdict.

**Counterexamples the reader and the rules must survive** (source-linked test input; not a claim that any commercial flow has passed):

- Empty file or `{}` — stage one exits non-zero through its parse and type checks: no envelope, no numeric value. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 10--22.
- Missing `unknowns`, an empty list, or a blank or non-string item — refusal `invalid local Library authoring-qualification input`. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 19--22.
- Blank or non-string `provenance` — the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, line 18.
- Malformed or non-64-hex `sourceSha256` — the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 14--15.
- Wrong `qualification` label or wrong `reportSchema` — the same refusal. Source: `flow/analyze-library-contract.sh`, lines 16--17.
- An envelope failing the reader's own five-field check — refusal `invalid local Library authoring-qualification result`, no value written. Source: `flow/read-library-contract.py`, lines 8--20.
- The shipped placeholder identity `aaaa...a` — format-valid, so it yields the typed value `1 count`; it must never be quoted as a verified source identity. Source: `flow/library-input.json`, line 2.
- A valid envelope carrying `0 count` — a declared test input, not producible by this flow's reader: constraint PASS, goal FAIL, not-ready ending. A true zero must never be read as success.
- Two candidate results, or an extra opaque success key — stage one rebuilds the envelope from exactly its five keys and the reader ignores anything else, so extras are dropped rather than chosen; the Act names exactly one input path and one envelope path, so a second candidate is never read. Declared limit: the refusal claim covers missing, malformed and blank fields only.

Knowledge: shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`, which turned the two command lines, the five fields and the fixed schema and label into a declared option list asserted before the count is read; by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`, which kept the constraint reading separate from the success target and made a `>= 0 count` PASS say nothing beyond closure at the tested conditions; by `one-checker-per-session.md`, which kept one tool and one option set so the reading belongs to the reader that produced it; and by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which made each refusal an ending the Pack declares rather than a silent zero.

## Run contract

**What a Site must bind and allow.**

- Named Site: `local` — local kind, ready, 1 parallel Job, 8 cores, 16 GiB, zero licence seats.
- A Site must provide `sh` and `python3` for the two declared wrapper lines below, read access to the flow copy and write access to the Campaign workspace. No licence is checked out and no commercial EDA tool is invoked.

**Inputs, each with its source identity.**

- `library-input.json` — the flow's own fixture, the single Campaign input. Its source identity is the file together with the 64-hex `sourceSha256` it carries; that value is the placeholder `aaaa...a`, recorded as asserted, not verified against any real source (declared limit). A changed input is a new Campaign.
- Flow root, read-only pointer, never copied into the Pack: `/private/tmp/hima-l4-AT8h3n/hima-home-OzRhpJ/workspace/library-authoring-source/flow`. The harness copies the pieces this contract names into the Campaign workspace; the Pack keeps no copy of any flow file.

**Outputs.**

- `libraryContract` — the declared reader-backed output, carrying the one typed value `library_contract_ready`, unit `count`. No other declared output exists.
- The envelope `library-insight.json` and the observation file are the two stages' intermediate files, not readings.

**Tools, each named with the exact wrapper that runs it.**

- Wrapper `analyze-library-contract`: `sh analyze-library-contract.sh library-input.json library-insight.json` — stage one of the flow, run on the copied flow; its input `library-input.json` is the fixture carried by that copy.
- Wrapper `read-library-contract`: `python3 read-library-contract.py library-insight.json observation.json` — stage two of the flow, run on the envelope stage one has just written; it produces the declared output `libraryContract`.

Both lines run exactly as the flow states them: no other tool, no second measurement, no generated code.

**Budget, and what bounds new attempts.**

- 1 generation.
- 1 retry, covering an execution or transport fault only: one attempt, never a second measurement, never a replacement for a first reading.
- 300 s wall clock.
- One Job at a time, matching the Site's single parallel Job; no licence seat.
- A refused input is final and is not retried. A further generation happens only as a new Campaign with a new fixed input identity.
- The scope statement this Pack must carry on every face lives in the Pack knowledge file `knowledge/scope-and-limits.md`; the field and option list asserted above lives in `knowledge/reading-the-contract.md`.

Knowledge: shaped by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`, which kept the flow where it lies and put pointers, not copies, in this contract; by `one-checker-per-session.md`, which kept one act node, one reader and one value; by `assert-the-checker-options.md`, which required the exact command lines to be written down; and by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which kept the attempt and generation limits in their place as a budget.

## Semantics

**One entry per typed value the readers produce.**

- **`library_contract_ready`** — unit `count`. Source: the flow's reader `read-library-contract.py`, writing into the declared output `libraryContract`. It measures whether the one bounded local authoring-qualification envelope validated: 64-hex identity, fixed `schema` `hima-library-insight-report/1`, label `authoring-qualification`, non-blank provenance, non-empty non-blank unknowns.
- **Typed values it can take:** `1` means present and valid. `0` means a valid envelope that is not ready, reachable only from a reader other than this flow's (declared limit).
- **Absence meaning:** the reader refused, so no value exists at all — no rule may PASS, and the refusal names the missing, malformed or blank field. A missing number is never a zero, and a typed `0` is never a refusal.
- **No other value exists:** `libraryContract` is the declared output that carries `library_contract_ready`, not a second value; the rule ids `library-contract-*`, the `schema` key, the `qualification` label and the placeholder identity are not readings, and no ratio, percentage or denominator is produced.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which named the value that detects each ending and kept "met exactly" distinct from "not measured at all"; by `one-checker-per-session.md`, which named the value after the tool that produced it and allowed only one; and by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`, which made a reported zero a measurement to report as itself rather than a pass.

## Judge rules

**Two ordered rules over the one declared value, constraint first and goal second, and what each verdict cites.**

- **Rule `library-contract-nonnegative`** (constraint), over `library_contract_ready`: PASS when the reading is `>= 0 count`; FAIL when the reading is below zero, which this flow's reader cannot produce (declared limit); UNDETERMINED when no value exists.
- **Rule `library-contract-goal`** (goal), over the same reading: PASS when it is `>= 1 count`, the bound goal; FAIL when it is `0 count`, a valid envelope that is not ready; UNDETERMINED when no value exists.
- **What each verdict cites:** the observation record of the declared output `libraryContract` — the typed value with its unit, plus the five validated envelope fields. A refusal verdict cites the reader's refusal text and names the offending field.
- **Routing:** constraint FAIL or UNDETERMINED goes to the wait node and the goal rule is not consulted. Constraint PASS with goal FAIL goes to the wait node. Constraint PASS with goal PASS goes to the chooser, which alone may record `goalMet`.
- A refused or absent reading is never converted into `0 count` and never into a goal result. A reading whose declared options were not the ones asserted has no verdict and becomes a blocker, not a conclusion.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which made every rule outcome that stops the Run one the Pack declares; by `assert-the-checker-options.md`, which put the verdict on the asserted option set rather than on a successful number; and by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`, which kept the constraint verdict from claiming anything beyond closure at the tested conditions.

## Choosers

**One chooser: the Explore `decide` node.**

- **What it reads:** the typed value `library_contract_ready` through the two ordered verdicts — the constraint verdict first, then the goal verdict.
- **What it sets:** `goalMet`, and only when the constraint verdict is PASS and the goal verdict is PASS. That decision ends the Run, and only after it may a TEST record be written.
- **What it sets on any other outcome:** nothing. FAIL or UNDETERMINED produces no chooser decision and goes to the declared wait/refusal path.
- **No converge block:** the Campaign runs one generation and the reading cannot move across generations, so no watched value, band or generation count is declared; convergence is unreachable here and no converged ending is declared.
- **No next strategy:** no strategy knob exists, so the chooser never proposes a move; a different input is a new Campaign.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which allowed only a fact-backed ending and made the chooser state in its own vocabulary that the goal is met; and by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`, which kept the flow as reference rather than objective, so the chooser aims at the Pack's bounded check and never at reproducing the flow.

## Endings

**Every way a Campaign of this Pack ends, in words, each named with what reaches it.**

1. **Goal met** — reached by the chooser clause that records `goalMet` on the goal rule's PASS after the constraint rule's PASS. The Run is terminal, and a TEST record may be written only after that decision.
2. **Refused input** — reached by the constraint rule's FAIL or UNDETERMINED routing to the wait node. The Run ends naming the missing, malformed or blank field and states that no success value exists.
3. **Valid but not ready** — reached by the constraint rule's PASS with the goal rule's FAIL on a typed `0 count`, routing to the wait node. The Run ends not-ready and is never converted into a goal result.

**Not endings.** The 1 generation / 1 retry / 300 s box is a budget: if it is ever reached, the report says the budget was exhausted with no conclusion, and it is not dressed up as an ending. A running or paused Run is not TEST evidence. Convergence is not declared here at all, because with one generation the reading cannot move and nothing watches a band.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which required every ending to be one this Pack declares in words and to have the value that detects it, and which kept the generation limit a budget rather than an ending.

## Workshops

**None.** No AI-authored code runs at run time: the Pack runs the flow's own two commands on the flow copy, and every reading comes from the flow's own reader. A Pack-local wrapper or reader written at authoring time is not a workshop, and none is needed here — an extra-key rejection check would exceed the flow's stated command line and output contract, so it is recorded as a declared limit instead of being generated at run time.

Knowledge: shaped by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`, which bound the Pack to the flow as it lies rather than generating a replacement for it.

## Knowledge

**Two Pack knowledge files, each named above as being for something.**

- **`knowledge/scope-and-limits.md`** — purpose: the scope statement the Pack must carry on every face — a local authoring-qualification check of one bounded input only, no Liberty, no QuaLib, no `edarun`, no production Library facts, no E1--E4 requalification, no customer data, no commercial qualification claimed, the source identity asserted rather than verified, and extra envelope keys dropped. Named by `## Run contract` and `## Goal template`.
- **`knowledge/reading-the-contract.md`** — purpose: the five required fields, the fixed schema and label, the reader's gate, and the counterexamples with their expected refusals and typed values, so a Model moment and the test record work from one list. Named by `## Run contract` and `## Constraints`.

No other Pack knowledge file is declared.

Knowledge: shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`, which put the declared field and option list in writing rather than leaving it assumed; and by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which kept the refusal wording beside the ending it belongs to.

Both lines run exactly as the flow states them: no other tool, no second measurement, no generated code.

**Budget, and what bounds new attempts.**

- 1 generation.
- 1 retry, covering an execution or transport fault only: one attempt, never a second measurement, never a replacement for a first reading.
- 300 s wall clock.
- One Job at a time, matching the Site's single parallel Job; no licence seat.
- A refused input is final and is not retried. A further generation happens only as a new Campaign with a new fixed input identity.
- The scope statement this Pack must carry on every face lives in the Pack knowledge file `knowledge/scope-and-limits.md`; the field and option list asserted above lives in `knowledge/reading-the-contract.md`.

Knowledge: shaped by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`, which kept the flow where it lies and put pointers, not copies, in this contract; by `one-checker-per-session.md`, which kept one act node, one reader and one value; by `assert-the-checker-options.md`, which required the exact command lines to be written down; and by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which kept the attempt and generation limits in their place as a budget.

## Semantics

**One entry per typed value the readers produce.**

- **`library_contract_ready`** — unit `count`. Source: the flow's reader `read-library-contract.py`, writing into the declared output `libraryContract`. It measures whether the one bounded local authoring-qualification envelope validated: 64-hex identity, fixed `schema` `hima-library-insight-report/1`, label `authoring-qualification`, non-blank provenance, non-empty non-blank unknowns.
- **Typed values it can take:** `1` means present and valid. `0` means a valid envelope that is not ready, reachable only from a reader other than this flow's (declared limit).
- **Absence meaning:** the reader refused, so no value exists at all — no rule may PASS, and the refusal names the missing, malformed or blank field. A missing number is never a zero, and a typed `0` is never a refusal.
- **No other value exists:** `libraryContract` is the declared output that carries `library_contract_ready`, not a second value; the rule ids `library-contract-*`, the `schema` key, the `qualification` label and the placeholder identity are not readings, and no ratio, percentage or denominator is produced.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which named the value that detects each ending and kept "met exactly" distinct from "not measured at all"; by `one-checker-per-session.md`, which named the value after the tool that produced it and allowed only one; and by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`, which made a reported zero a measurement to report as itself rather than a pass.

## Judge rules

**Two ordered rules over the one declared value, constraint first and goal second, and what each verdict cites.**

- **Rule `library-contract-nonnegative`** (constraint), over `library_contract_ready`: PASS when the reading is `>= 0 count`; FAIL when the reading is below zero, which this flow's reader cannot produce (declared limit); UNDETERMINED when no value exists.
- **Rule `library-contract-goal`** (goal), over the same reading: PASS when it is `>= 1 count`, the bound goal; FAIL when it is `0 count`, a valid envelope that is not ready; UNDETERMINED when no value exists.
- **What each verdict cites:** the observation record of the declared output `libraryContract` — the typed value with its unit, plus the five validated envelope fields. A refusal verdict cites the reader's refusal text and names the offending field.
- **Routing:** constraint FAIL or UNDETERMINED goes to the wait node and the goal rule is not consulted. Constraint PASS with goal FAIL goes to the wait node. Constraint PASS with goal PASS goes to the chooser, which alone may record `goalMet`.
- A refused or absent reading is never converted into `0 count` and never into a goal result. A reading whose declared options were not the ones asserted has no verdict and becomes a blocker, not a conclusion.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which made every rule outcome that stops the Run one the Pack declares; by `assert-the-checker-options.md`, which put the verdict on the asserted option set rather than on a successful number; and by `over-constrain-and-read-the-violation.md`, which kept the constraint verdict from claiming anything beyond closure at the tested conditions.

## Choosers

**One chooser: the Explore `decide` node.**

- **What it reads:** the typed value `library_contract_ready` through the two ordered verdicts — the constraint verdict first, then the goal verdict.
- **What it sets:** `goalMet`, and only when the constraint verdict is PASS and the goal verdict is PASS. That decision ends the Run, and only after it may a TEST record be written.
- **What it sets on any other outcome:** nothing. FAIL or UNDETERMINED produces no chooser decision and goes to the declared wait/refusal path.
- **No converge block:** the Campaign runs one generation and the reading cannot move across generations, so no watched value, band or generation count is declared; convergence is unreachable here and no converged ending is declared.
- **No next strategy:** no strategy knob exists, so the chooser never proposes a move; a different input is a new Campaign.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which allowed only a fact-backed ending and made the chooser state in its own vocabulary that the goal is met; and by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`, which kept the flow as reference rather than objective, so the chooser aims at the Pack's bounded check and never at reproducing the flow.

## Endings

**Every way a Campaign of this Pack ends, in words, each named with what reaches it.**

1. **Goal met** — reached by the chooser clause that records `goalMet` on the goal rule's PASS after the constraint rule's PASS. The Run is terminal, and a TEST record may be written only after that decision.
2. **Refused input** — reached by the constraint rule's FAIL or UNDETERMINED routing to the wait node. The Run ends naming the missing, malformed or blank field and states that no success value exists.
3. **Valid but not ready** — reached by the constraint rule's PASS with the goal rule's FAIL on a typed `0 count`, routing to the wait node. The Run ends not-ready and is never converted into a goal result.

**Not endings.** The 1 generation / 1 retry / 300 s box is a budget: if it is ever reached, the report says the budget was exhausted with no conclusion, and it is not dressed up as an ending. A running or paused Run is not TEST evidence. Convergence is not declared here at all, because with one generation the reading cannot move and nothing watches a band.

Knowledge: shaped by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which required every ending to be one this Pack declares in words and to have the value that detects it, and which kept the generation limit a budget rather than an ending.

## Workshops

**None.** No AI-authored code runs at run time: the Pack runs the flow's own two commands on the flow copy, and every reading comes from the flow's own reader. A Pack-local wrapper or reader written at authoring time is not a workshop, and none is needed here — an extra-key rejection check would exceed the flow's stated command line and output contract, so it is recorded as a declared limit instead of being generated at run time.

Knowledge: shaped by `what-a-golden-flow-is.md`, which bound the Pack to the flow as it lies rather than generating a replacement for it.

## Knowledge

**Two Pack knowledge files, each named above as being for something.**

- **`knowledge/scope-and-limits.md`** — purpose: the scope statement the Pack must carry on every face — a local authoring-qualification check of one bounded input only, no Liberty, no QuaLib, no `edarun`, no production Library facts, no E1--E4 requalification, no customer data, no commercial qualification claimed, the source identity asserted rather than verified, and extra envelope keys dropped. Named by `## Run contract` and `## Goal template`.
- **`knowledge/reading-the-contract.md`** — purpose: the five required fields, the fixed schema and label, the reader's gate, and the counterexamples with their expected refusals and typed values, so a Model moment and the test record work from one list. Named by `## Run contract` and `## Constraints`.

No other Pack knowledge file is declared.

Knowledge: shaped by `assert-the-checker-options.md`, which put the declared field and option list in writing rather than leaving it assumed; and by `end-honestly-in-more-than-one-way.md`, which kept the refusal wording beside the ending it belongs to.

1: # What a pack folder holds, file by file
2: 
3: The skeleton the fabric stage compiles to. Every block below is the **smallest file of its kind that
4: this harness accepts**, with one note per field saying what that field is for. Nothing here is a
5: method: the ids, the paths, the units and the numbers are stand-ins, and what they should be for the
6: pack you are writing is the spec's to say and never this file's.
7: 
8: Read this for shape. Read the pack installed beside the folder you are authoring for a whole example
9: of the first two, written by hand for a real business. Ask `hima_pack_check` whether what you wrote
10: is a pack: it names every fault in the pack's own files, and that answer is the authority no
11: skeleton can be.
12: 
13: A pack folder holds, at its top: `contract.yml`, `graph.yml`, `semantics.yml` where the pack's own
14: readers emit value types, and the directories `rules/`, `choosers/`, `readers/`, `knowledge/` and
15: `tools/` where it has files for them. Every path in it is a plain file with a plain name — no link,
16: no hidden name, nothing but letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores in each segment.
17: 
18: ## `contract.yml` — what a Site must bind, what a generation produces, what the pack runs
19: 
20: ```yaml
21: id: example-probe            # the folder's own name; lowercase letters, digits and dashes
22: version: '1'                 # a string, and graph.yml states the same one
23: title: Example probe         # what a person reads the pack under
24: 
25: inputs:                      # what a Site binds in its own site file; the pack binds none of them
26:   - name: flowRoot
27:     description: The Golden Flow's root on the Site. Read where it lies, never written.
28:   - name: design
29:     description: What the flow is run over, spelled as the flow's own manifests spell it.
30:   - name: workspaceRoot
31:     description: Where campaign workspaces are made; the Site's permit must allow writes under it.
32: 
33: outputs:                     # what a generation leaves in its own workspace
34:   - name: measurement
35:     path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt   # relative to the workspace; ${…} is an input above
36:     reader: measurement-file                    # the reader that turns it into typed values
37:     description: What this generation measured. The judged file.
38:   - name: toolLog
39:     path: flow/logs/${design}/tool.log         # no reader: a file a person reads after a failure
40:     description: What the tool said while it ran.
41: 
42: environment:
43:   wrappers:                  # the first word of every command line below — a tool's argv[0] and a
44:     - make                   #   reader's; the Site's permit decides each, and a word not here is
45:     - sh                     #   refused before a campaign starts
46: 
47: workspace:
48:   copy:                      # what is copied out of flowRoot into <workspace>/flow/, once per campaign
49:     - Makefile
50:     - tools
51:     - inputs/${design}
52: 
53: tools:
54:   - id: measure
55:     file: tools/measure.sh   # the script a person can run by hand, under this folder's tools/
56:     description: One generation of the flow's own measuring stage, in the campaign's copy of it.
57:     inputs: [WORKSPACE, DESIGN, STEP_MS]   # the variables the script reads, and the only names argv may use
58:     licences:                # optional: what a job of this tool holds on the Site while it runs
59:       measuring-seat: 1      # the Site declares how many it has; a tool that holds none writes no block
60:     argv:                    # what the harness launches; argv[0] is the wrapper above
61:       - make
62:       - -C
63:       - ${WORKSPACE}/flow
64:       - DESIGN=${DESIGN}
65:       - measure
66:       - STEP_MS=${STEP_MS}
67: 
68: rules:                       # the judge rules this pack may apply, by id: this folder's rules/ first,
69:   - measurement-within-bound #   the bundle's second
70: 
71: knowledge:                   # optional: this pack's own domain knowledge, one entry per file
72:   - file: the-step-method.md
73:     purpose: why this pack changes the step the way it does
74: 
75: strategy:                    # what a run is set to for one generation; at least one knob, each whole
76:   stepMs: { type: number, unit: ms, min: 0.5, max: 10, default: 2 }
77:   shape: { type: choice, options: [plain, dense], default: plain }
78: 
79: words:                       # what a person reads each number under: one entry per goal parameter the
80:   measurement_at_most: { label: measurement at most, unit: ms }   # graph binds, one per knob above
81:   stepMs: { label: step, unit: ms }
82:   shape: { label: shape }    # a choice states no unit: a choice is measured in nothing
83: ```
84: 
85: ## Workshop declaration and graph binding
86: 
87: A Workshop is an existing `act` node variant. Its input reports are contract `outputs` produced by
88: earlier nodes; scalar `inputs` are bound by the node. Knowledge files also appear in the contract's
89: `knowledge`. The following is an additional block within `contract.yml`, not a separate file:
90: 
91: ```yaml
92: outputs:
93:   - name: measuredInput
94:     path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt
95:     reader: measurement-file
96:     description: The preceding tool's measurement.
97:   - name: analysis
98:     path: research/analysis/result.txt
99:     reader: measurement-file
100:     description: The script's derived measurement, checked by the reader and Judge.
101: environment:
102:   wrappers: [sh]
103: knowledge:
104:   - file: analysis-method.md
105:     purpose: How the measurements support the analysis.
106: workshops:
107:   - id: analyze
108:     purpose: Read measuredInput and write a script deriving the requested measurement from its actual data.
109:     directory: research/analysis
110:     entry: entry.sh
111:     language: sh
112:     inputs: [LIMIT]
113:     reads: [measuredInput]
114:     knowledge: [analysis-method.md]
115:     produces: analysis
116:     argv: [sh, '${ENTRY}', '${WORKSPACE}', '${LIMIT}']
117:     licences: {}             # omit when no licensed resource is needed
118: ```
119: 
120: The corresponding graph node and downstream read are real nodes, connected after the input producer:
121: 
122: ```yaml
123: - id: analyze
124:   kind: act
125:   parameters:
126:     workshop: analyze
127:     arguments:
128:       LIMIT: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
129: - id: read-analysis
130:   kind: act
131:   parameters:
132:     observes: analysis
133: ```
134: 
135: `reads` and `produces` are exact `contract.outputs[].name` values. The model's read tool takes that
136: same output name. `@workshop-input:<name>` is an internal diagnostic label; it is not a declared
137: output, path, or read argument. `produces` names an output, not the value type its reader emits.
138: The output's reader emits types declared by `semantics.yml`; downstream Judge rules consume those
139: types. `directory` is relative to the Campaign workspace and cannot be `flow` or the readers'
140: reserved directory. `entry` is one filename. `argv[0]` is a declared Site wrapper, and `argv[1]`
141: is exactly `${ENTRY}`. A script may produce a declared output elsewhere in the Campaign workspace;
142: its code-writing tool is confined to the admitted code directory. Neither may escape the Site permit.
143: 
144: | Operand | Meaning for a controlled execution |
145: | --- | --- |
146: | `${ENTRY}` | The generated entry script inside this execution's private code directory. |
147: | `${WORKSPACE}` | The Campaign root containing `flow/` and the declared output paths. |
148: | `${WORKSHOP}` | This execution's private code directory beneath the declared `directory`, including its execution identity. |
149: 
150: This example passes `WORKSPACE`, so shell `$1` is the Campaign root and `$2` is LIMIT. Its input
151: and output paths start from `$1`. A script needing helper files in its private code directory may
152: also need a `WORKSHOP` operand; use the approved spec's exact operand order and document each shell
153: position. Obtain the Campaign root from `WORKSPACE`, never by assuming a number of parent directories
154: above `WORKSHOP`. The example supplies file shape, not permission to replace the spec's argv.
155: 
156: Reader scripts have their own argv: below `$1` is `${REPORT}` and `$2` is `${OUT}`. These are argv
157: arrays; shell commands, pipes and redirections belong inside scripts.
158: 
159: ## `graph.yml` — the four node kinds, the outcomes the edges are taken on, and the one edge back
160: 
161: The block illustrates node and edge syntax. For an executable Explore method, supply the actual
162: constraint and Goal rules from the spec: the preceding Judge needs at least two ordered rules,
163: constraint first and Goal second. The single rule skeleton here does not supply that whole method.
164: 
165: ```yaml
166: id: example-probe            # the contract's id
167: version: '1'                 # the contract's version
168: entry: measure               # the node a campaign starts at
169: 
170: nodes:
171:   - id: measure              # act: run one of the contract's tools on the Site and wait for it
172:     kind: act
173:     parameters:
174:       tool: measure
175:       arguments:             # what the Run supplies for this generation
176:         STEP_MS: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
177: 
178:   - id: read-measurement     # act: read one of the contract's outputs into the ledger
179:     kind: act
180:     parameters:
181:       observes: measurement
182: 
183:   - id: judge                # judge: apply rules in order; the edge out is chosen by the first one's outcome
184:     kind: judge
185:     parameters:
186:       rules: [measurement-within-bound]
187:       bind:                  # what binds each parameter a rule declares
188:         bound_ms: { from: goal, name: measurement_at_most }
189: 
190:   - id: next-step            # explore: choose the next strategy, or open a loop of its own
191:     kind: explore
192:     parameters:
193:       chooser: step-back-off # by id, exactly as a rule is named
194:       bind:                  # the numbers the chooser leaves to the pack author
195:         marginMs: 0.05
196:       converge:              # optional, and all four together: when this loop has stopped learning
197:         read: measured       # one of the chooser's own `reads`
198:         band: 0.05           # how far apart two generations must be to count as movement
199:         generations: 1       # how many successive generations must have moved by less than that
200:         generationLimit: 6   # what this pack thinks a campaign of it should be allowed at most
201: 
202:   - id: blocked              # wait: where a run stops for a person once its retries are spent
203:     kind: wait
204:     parameters:
205:       blocker: hard-blocker
206: 
207: edges:
208:   - { from: measure, to: read-measurement }            # an act node's one unlabelled edge out
209:   - { from: read-measurement, to: judge }
210:   - { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: PASS }      # a judge node's edges carry their outcome
211:   - { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: FAIL }
212:   - { from: next-step, to: measure, revisit: true }    # the loop: the only edge that goes back
213: ```
214: 
215: Read actual edges to audit endings. Judge routing uses the first rule's outcome, while an Explore
216: owner decision uses the current required Judge evidence. A goal-met decision ends the Run before a
217: revisit; a next-strategy decision follows the revisit only if the original generation budget allows
218: it. A terminal Judge PASS alone supplies no Campaign goal-met decision. Waits remain legitimate
219: where the approved spec calls for human clearance; compare each actual outcome path with that spec.
220: Comments such as "PASS is terminal" cannot override a PASS edge whose destination is a wait node.
221: 
222: ## `semantics.yml` — what the value types this pack's own readers emit mean
223: 
224: Written **only** where this pack's own readers emit a value type. A pack whose outputs are all read
225: by readers the harness ships declares none and writes no such file.
226: 
227: The two qualifier vocabularies are the harness's own and are **fixed**: `mode` is `setup` or `hold`,
228: `scope` is `all` or `reg2reg`. Declaring either means every reading of that type carries one of the
229: listed words; declaring neither means a reading of it carries no qualifier at all.
230: 
231: ```yaml
232: values:
233:   measured_ms:               # the slug a reader emits and a rule or chooser reads
234:     unit: ms                 # what a value of it is measured in; every reading is held to this
235:     mode: [setup, hold]      # optional: the analysis passes a value of it can belong to
236:     scope: [all, reg2reg]    # optional: the path groups a value of it can cover
237:     description: what this generation measured, as the file states it
238: ```
239: 
240: ## `rules/<id>.yml` — one judge rule
241: 
242: ```yaml
243: id: measurement-within-bound # the file's own name, without the .yml
244: version: '1'
245: title: The measurement is within the bound the run was started with
246: parameter:                   # optional: the one value a node binds at judge time
247:   name: bound_ms
248:   unit: ms
249: requires:                    # what must have been observed for this rule to have an opinion at all
250:   - type: measured_ms
251: subject:                     # the value the predicate is about
252:   type: measured_ms
253: predicate:
254:   op: lte                    # lte, gte and the like
255:   threshold: { parameter: bound_ms }   # or a number written here
256:   unit: ms
257: ```
258: 
259: ## `choosers/<id>.yml` — one explore move, as data
260: 
261: ```yaml
262: id: step-back-off
263: version: '1'
264: title: Take the step back by what the last generation missed by
265: parameter:                   # the one number the pack binds in its explore node's `bind:`
266:   name: marginMs
267:   unit: ms
268: reads:                       # what is read out of the run's latest observation, by type
269:   measured: { type: measured_ms, unit: ms }
270: decide:                      # first matching clause wins
271:   - when: { constraint: PASS, goal: PASS }
272:     goalMet: true            # the goal is reached; there is no next strategy
273:   - when: { constraint: PASS }
274:     next:                    # sets this pack's own strategy knobs by name; a knob not named carries over
275:       stepMs: { sum: [measured, marginMs] }
276:   - when: { constraint: FAIL }
277:     next:
278:       stepMs: { sum: [measured, { neg: marginMs }] }
279: ```
280: 
281: ## `readers/<id>.yml` and its script under `tools/` — a reader of this pack's own
282: 
283: ```yaml
284: id: measurement-file
285: version: '1'
286: file: tools/read-measurement.sh   # under this folder's tools/, and a plain file
287: argv:                             # every word is a literal, or exactly one of the four placeholders
288:   - sh                            # argv[0] is the wrapper: a literal word the contract declares
289:   - ${READER}                     # the script's path on the Site
290:   - ${REPORT}                     # the output the contract pointed it at
291:   - ${OUT}                        # the file the script must write

lines.text: # What a pack folder holds, file by file
The skeleton the fabric stage compiles to. Every block below is the **smallest file of its kind that
this harness accepts**, with one note per field saying what that field is for. Nothing here is a
method: the ids, the paths, the units and the numbers are stand-ins, and what they should be for the
pack you are writing is the spec's to say and never this file's.
Read this for shape. Read the pack installed beside the folder you are authoring for a whole example
of the first two, written by hand for a real business. Ask `hima_pack_check` whether what you wrote
is a pack: it names every fault in the pack's own files, and that answer is the authority no
skeleton can be.
A pack folder holds, at its top: `contract.yml`, `graph.yml`, `semantics.yml` where the pack's own
readers emit value types, and the directories `rules/`, `choosers/`, `readers/`, `knowledge/` and
`tools/` where it has files for them. Every path in it is a plain file with a plain name — no link,
no hidden name, nothing but letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores in each segment.
## `contract.yml` — what a Site must bind, what a generation produces, what the pack runs
```yaml
id: example-probe            # the folder's own name; lowercase letters, digits and dashes
version: '1'                 # a string, and graph.yml states the same one
title: Example probe         # what a person reads the pack under
inputs:                      # what a Site binds in its own site file; the pack binds none of them
- name: flowRoot
description: The Golden Flow's root on the Site. Read where it lies, never written.
- name: design
description: What the flow is run over, spelled as the flow's own manifests spell it.
- name: workspaceRoot
description: Where campaign workspaces are made; the Site's permit must allow writes under it.
outputs:                     # what a generation leaves in its own workspace
- name: measurement
path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt   # relative to the workspace; ${…} is an input above
reader: measurement-file                    # the reader that turns it into typed values
description: What this generation measured. The judged file.
- name: toolLog
path: flow/logs/${design}/tool.log         # no reader: a file a person reads after a failure
description: What the tool said while it ran.
environment:
wrappers:                  # the first word of every command line below — a tool's argv[0] and a
- make                   #   reader's; the Site's permit decides each, and a word not here is
- sh                     #   refused before a campaign starts
workspace:
copy:                      # what is copied out of flowRoot into <workspace>/flow/, once per campaign
- Makefile
- tools
- inputs/${design}
tools:
- id: measure
file: tools/measure.sh   # the script a person can run by hand, under this folder's tools/
description: One generation of the flow's own measuring stage, in the campaign's copy of it.
inputs: [WORKSPACE, DESIGN, STEP_MS]   # the variables the script reads, and the only names argv may use
licences:                # optional: what a job of this tool holds on the Site while it runs
measuring-seat: 1      # the Site declares how many it has; a tool that holds none writes no block
argv:                    # what the harness launches; argv[0] is the wrapper above
- make
- ${WORKSPACE}/flow
- DESIGN=${DESIGN}
- measure
- STEP_MS=${STEP_MS}
rules:                       # the judge rules this pack may apply, by id: this folder's rules/ first,
- measurement-within-bound #   the bundle's second
knowledge:                   # optional: this pack's own domain knowledge, one entry per file
- file: the-step-method.md
purpose: why this pack changes the step the way it does
strategy:                    # what a run is set to for one generation; at least one knob, each whole
stepMs: { type: number, unit: ms, min: 0.5, max: 10, default: 2 }
shape: { type: choice, options: [plain, dense], default: plain }
words:                       # what a person reads each number under: one entry per goal parameter the
measurement_at_most: { label: measurement at most, unit: ms }   # graph binds, one per knob above
stepMs: { label: step, unit: ms }
shape: { label: shape }    # a choice states no unit: a choice is measured in nothing
## Workshop declaration and graph binding
A Workshop is an existing `act` node variant. Its input reports are contract `outputs` produced by
earlier nodes; scalar `inputs` are bound by the node. Knowledge files also appear in the contract's
`knowledge`. The following is an additional block within `contract.yml`, not a separate file:
```yaml
outputs:
- name: measuredInput
path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt
reader: measurement-file
description: The preceding tool's measurement.
- name: analysis
path: research/analysis/result.txt
reader: measurement-file
description: The script's derived measurement, checked by the reader and Judge.
environment:
wrappers: [sh]
knowledge:
- file: analysis-method.md
purpose: How the measurements support the analysis.
workshops:
- id: analyze
purpose: Read measuredInput and write a script deriving the requested measurement from its actual data.
directory: research/analysis
entry: entry.sh
language: sh
inputs: [LIMIT]
reads: [measuredInput]
knowledge: [analysis-method.md]
produces: analysis
argv: [sh, '${ENTRY}', '${WORKSPACE}', '${LIMIT}']
licences: {}             # omit when no licensed resource is needed

```yaml

kind: act
parameters:
workshop: analyze
arguments:
LIMIT: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }

kind: act
parameters:
observes: analysis

| Operand | Meaning for a controlled execution |
| `${ENTRY}` | The generated entry script inside this execution's private code directory. |
| `${WORKSPACE}` | The Campaign root containing `flow/` and the declared output paths. |
| `${WORKSHOP}` | This execution's private code directory beneath the declared `directory`, including its execution identity. |

## `graph.yml` — the four node kinds, the outcomes the edges are taken on, and the one edge back

constraint and Goal rules from the spec: the preceding Judge needs at least two ordered rules,
constraint first and Goal second. The single rule skeleton here does not supply that whole method.
```yaml
id: example-probe            # the contract's id
version: '1'                 # the contract's version
entry: measure               # the node a campaign starts at
nodes:
- id: measure              # act: run one of the contract's tools on the Site and wait for it
kind: act
parameters:
tool: measure
arguments:             # what the Run supplies for this generation
STEP_MS: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
- id: read-measurement     # act: read one of the contract's outputs into the ledger
kind: act
parameters:
observes: measurement
- id: judge                # judge: apply rules in order; the edge out is chosen by the first one's outcome
kind: judge
parameters:
rules: [measurement-within-bound]
bind:                  # what binds each parameter a rule declares
bound_ms: { from: goal, name: measurement_at_most }
- id: next-step            # explore: choose the next strategy, or open a loop of its own
kind: explore
parameters:
chooser: step-back-off # by id, exactly as a rule is named
bind:                  # the numbers the chooser leaves to the pack author
marginMs: 0.05
converge:              # optional, and all four together: when this loop has stopped learning
read: measured       # one of the chooser's own `reads`
band: 0.05           # how far apart two generations must be to count as movement
generations: 1       # how many successive generations must have moved by less than that
generationLimit: 6   # what this pack thinks a campaign of it should be allowed at most

kind: wait
parameters:
blocker: hard-blocker
edges:
- { from: measure, to: read-measurement }            # an act node's one unlabelled edge out
- { from: read-measurement, to: judge }
- { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: PASS }      # a judge node's edges carry their outcome
- { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: FAIL }
- { from: next-step, to: measure, revisit: true }    # the loop: the only edge that goes back

owner decision uses the current required Judge evidence. A goal-met decision ends the Run before a
revisit; a next-strategy decision follows the revisit only if the original generation budget allows
it. A terminal Judge PASS alone supplies no Campaign goal-met decision. Waits remain legitimate
where the approved spec calls for human clearance; compare each actual outcome path with that spec.
Comments such as "PASS is terminal" cannot override a PASS edge whose destination is a wait node.
## `semantics.yml` — what the value types this pack's own readers emit mean
Written **only** where this pack's own readers emit a value type. A pack whose outputs are all read
by readers the harness ships declares none and writes no such file.

`scope` is `all` or `reg2reg`. Declaring either means every reading of that type carries one of the
listed words; declaring neither means a reading of it carries no qualifier at all.

values:
measured_ms:               # the slug a reader emits and a rule or chooser reads
unit: ms                 # what a value of it is measured in; every reading is held to this
mode: [setup, hold]      # optional: the analysis passes a value of it can belong to
scope: [all, reg2reg]    # optional: the path groups a value of it can cover

version: '1'
title: The measurement is within the bound the run was started with

name: bound_ms
unit: ms
requires:                    # what must have been observed for this rule to have an opinion at all
- type: measured_ms
subject:                     # the value the predicate is about
type: measured_ms
predicate:
op: lte                    # lte, gte and the like
threshold: { parameter: bound_ms }   # or a number written here

title: Take the step back by what the last generation missed by

owner decision uses the current required Judge evidence. A goal-met decision ends the Run before a
revisit; a next-strategy decision follows the revisit only if the original generation budget allows
it. A terminal Judge PASS alone supplies no Campaign goal-met decision. Waits remain legitimate
where the approved spec calls for human clearance; compare each actual outcome path with that spec.
Comments such as "PASS is terminal" cannot override a PASS edge whose destination is a wait node.

Written **only** where this pack's own readers emit a value type. A pack whose outputs are all read
by readers the harness ships declares none and writes no such file.

`scope` is `all` or `reg2reg`. Declaring either means every reading of that type carries one of the
listed words; declaring neither means a reading of it carries no qualifier at all.

values:
measured_ms:               # the slug a reader emits and a rule or chooser reads
unit: ms                 # what a value of it is measured in; every reading is held to this

scope: [all, reg2reg]    # optional: the path groups a value of it can cover
description: what this generation measured, as the file states it

version: '1'
title: The measurement is within the bound the run was started with
parameter:                   # optional: the one value a node binds at judge time
name: bound_ms
unit: ms
requires:                    # what must have been observed for this rule to have an opinion at all
- type: measured_ms
subject:                     # the value the predicate is about
type: measured_ms
predicate:
op: lte                    # lte, gte and the like
threshold: { parameter: bound_ms }   # or a number written here
unit: ms

version: '1'
title: Take the step back by what the last generation missed by
parameter:                   # the one number the pack binds in its explore node's `bind:`
name: marginMs
unit: ms
reads:                       # what is read out of the run's latest observation, by type
measured: { type: measured_ms, unit: ms }
decide:                      # first matching clause wins
- when: { constraint: PASS, goal: PASS }
goalMet: true            # the goal is reached; there is no next strategy
- when: { constraint: PASS }
next:                    # sets this pack's own strategy knobs by name; a knob not named carries over
stepMs: { sum: [measured, marginMs] }
- when: { constraint: FAIL }

stepMs: { sum: [measured, { neg: marginMs }] }

```yaml

version: '1'
file: tools/read-measurement.sh   # under this folder's tools/, and a plain file

- ${READER}                     # the script's path on the Site

A plain Markdown file, one per entry of the contract's `knowledge:`, written for the purpose that
entry gives it. It guides the executing Agent; it does not establish measured facts. Explain the
method symbolically. Include a worked numeric result only with the exact input and parameters and
an observed calculation or checked result that produced it; otherwise leave the result unverified.
An example value copied from another dataset cannot serve as this dataset's expected answer.
```markdown

<the reasoning, in the author's own words, for the purpose the contract declares>

authoring account and not the pack — no campaign reads one — and the digest of the files a campaign
runs is taken without them.
| File | Written by | Sections, in this order |
| `INTENT.md` | `/hima-grill` | `Business`, `Golden Flow`, `Answers`, `Ambiguities resolved`, `Knowledge applied` |
| `SPEC.md` | `/hima-spec` | `Goal template`, `Constraints`, `Run contract`, `Semantics`, `Judge rules`, `Choosers`, `Endings`, `Workshops`, `Knowledge` |
| `FABRIC.md` | `/hima-fabric` | `Files written`, `Gaps`, `Reviews` |
| `TEST.md` | `/hima-test` | `Site`, `Run`, `Ending`, `Generations`, `Code`, `Refusals`, `Disagreements` |
| `VERSION.yml` | `/hima-release`, through the harness's own verb | `pack`, `version`, `released`, `test: { record, run }`, `files:` — one sha256 per file |

nothing extra, nothing twice, nothing out of order, nothing empty. `VERSION.yml` is the one of the
five nobody writes by hand: every hash in it is computed by the harness over the bytes in the folder.
